insight.title: Why Cozy Online Groups Always Implode
insight.subtitle: The coziest corners of the internet eventually face bitter civil wars over the most insignificant things.
insight.notificationHook: Why cozy online groups always implode

sections.text: You join a niche group for something wholesome—like sourdough baking or mechanical keyboards. But eventually, the community fractures into a bitter civil war over a minor rule or a slightly controversial post.

This happens because micro-communities offer high intimacy but low stakes. When there are no real-world consequences, members channel all their emotional energy into defending incredibly specific, unwritten cultural boundaries.
The result is a predictable lifecycle: a cozy haven gets popular, enters a purist phase, suffers a dramatic schism, and births three new, even more hyper-specific spin-off groups.
Every digital utopia is one bad moderator away from a civil war.
